components.title: The Water Cycle
components.subtitle: How water moves between the oceans, atmosphere, and land

components.text: The Sun heats water at the surface of oceans, lakes, and rivers. Water molecules gain energy, turn into vapour, and rise into the atmosphere.
As warm, moist air rises it cools. Water vapour condenses onto tiny particles such as dust, forming droplets that cluster into clouds.
When droplets grow heavy enough they fall as rain, snow, sleet, or hail. Water then collects in lakes, rivers, groundwater, and oceans, and the cycle begins again.

components.title: Worked example: a puddle after rain
components.body: A puddle forms on a warm afternoon after a storm. Sunlight heats the water, so it evaporates into the air (evaporation). The vapour cools higher up and forms a small cloud (condensation). Later, that cloud releases rain back onto the ground (precipitation).
components.takeaway: Every drop of water is part of a continuous loop, not a one-way trip.

questions.question: What drives evaporation in the water cycle?
questions.explanation: Solar energy heats surface water, giving molecules enough energy to become vapour.

questions.question: What is condensation?
options: Water vapour turning into liquid droplets
questions.explanation: Cooling water vapour condenses onto particles to form droplets and clouds.

questions.question: Which process returns water from clouds to the Earth's surface?
questions.explanation: Precipitation includes rain, snow, sleet, and hail falling from clouds.
